zh: 两人并坐低声谈了好一会方始结束。胡雪岩戴了一顶风帽，帽檐压得极低，带了一个叫阿福的伶俐小厮，打开花园中一道很少开启的便门，出门是一条长巷，巷子里没有什么行人，就是有，亦因这天冷得格外厉害，而且西北风很大，都是低头疾行，谁也没有发觉。这位平时出门，前呼后拥的胡财神，竞会踽踽凉凉地只带一个小厮步行上街。“阿福，”胡雪岩问道：“周老爷住在哪里，你晓得不晓得？”“怎么不晓得？他住在龙舌嘴。”“对！龙知嘴。”胡雪岩说：“你走快一点，通知他我要去。”“是。”阿福问道：“如果他不在家呢？”“这么冷的天，他不会出门的。”胡雪岩又说：“万一不在，你留句话，回来了到城隍山药王庙旁边的馆子里来寻我。”阿福答应一声，迈开大步往前走。胡雪岩安步当车，缓缓行去。刚进了龙舌嘴，只见阿福已经走回头路了，发现主人，急急迎了上来。“怎么样，不在家？”“在！”阿福回头一指：“那不是！”原来周少棠特为赶了来迎接。见了面，胡雪岩摇摇手，使个眼色。周少棠会意，他是怕在声招呼，惊动了路人，所以见了面，低声问道，“你怎么会来的？”
en: The two sat side by side and talked in low voices for a long time before they finished. Hu put on a hooded winter cap, pulling its brim very low, and took a quick-witted servant called A’fu with him. They opened a seldom-used side gate in the garden and stepped into a long lane. Few people were about, and those who were kept their heads down and hurried along: the cold was unusually severe, with a strong northwesterly wind. Nobody noticed that the God of Wealth, ordinarily surrounded by attendants whenever he went out, was trudging forlornly through the streets with only a single servant. “A’fu, do you know where Mr Zhou lives?” “Of course. At Longshezui.” “Yes, Longshezui. Go ahead and tell him I am coming.” “Yes, sir. What if he is not at home?” “He will not have gone out in weather like this. But if he has, leave word that when he returns he should come and find me at the restaurant beside Yaowang Temple on City God Hill.” A’fu strode ahead. Hu followed slowly on foot. He had barely entered Longshezui when he saw A’fu coming back. Catching sight of his master, the servant hurried towards him. “Well? Is he out?” “No!” A’fu pointed behind him. “There he is!” Zhou had come out specially to meet him. Hu waved a hand and gave him a warning look. Understanding that he feared a loud greeting would attract passers-by, Zhou asked quietly, “What brings you here?”

zh: 这话问得胡雪岩无以为答，笑笑答说：“你没有想到吧？”“真是没有想到，”胡雪岩发觉已经有人在注意了，便放快了脚步，反而走在周少棠前面，一直到巷口才停住步，抬头看了一下说：“你府上有二十年没有来过了。我记得是坐南朝北第五家。”“搬到对面去了，坐北朝南第四家。”“不错，不错！你后来买了你对面的房子，不过，我还是头一回来。”“这房子风水不好。”何以风水不好？胡雪岩一时无法追问，因为已到了周家。周少棠的妻子，胡雪岩还是二十几年前见过，记得很清楚的是，生得非常富态，如今更加发福，一双小足撑持着水牛般的身躯，行动非常艰难，但因胡雪岩“降尊纡贵”，在她便觉受宠若惊，满脸堆笑，非常殷勤。
en: Hu could find no answer. He smiled. “You did not expect me, did you?” “Certainly not.” Noticing that people were already looking, Hu quickened his pace and went ahead of Zhou. Only at the mouth of the lane did he stop and look up. “It is twenty years since I visited your house. I remember: the fifth house, facing north.” “We moved to the other side. The fourth house, facing south.” “Of course! You bought the house opposite. This will be my first visit there.” “The house has bad feng shui.” Why bad? Hu had no chance to ask, for they had arrived. He had last seen Mrs Zhou more than twenty years before. What he remembered most clearly was her substantial figure. She had grown still stouter: a pair of tiny bound feet supported a body as large as a buffalo, making movement difficult. Yet she was overwhelmed that Hu should condescend to visit, and attended to him with a face full of smiles.

zh: “不敢当，不敢当！”胡雪岩看亲自来敬茶，摇摇晃晃，脚步不稳，真担心她会摔交，所以老实说道：“周大嫂，不要招呼，你法身太重，掼一交不是当耍的。”“是不是！你真好省省了。胡大先生肯到我们这里来，是当我们自己人看待，你一客气，反而见外了。”周少棠又说：“有事叫阿春、阿秋来做。”原来周少棠从受了胡雪岩的提携，境遇日佳，他又喜欢讲排场，老夫妇两口，倒有四个佣人，阿春、阿秋是十年前买来的两个丫头，如今都快二十岁了。“恭敬不如从命。”周太太气喘吁吁地坐了下来，跟胡雪岩寒暄：“老太太精神倒还健旺？”“托福，托福。”“胡太太好？”“还好。”看样子还要问螺蛳太太跟姨太太。周少棠已经知道了胡家这天上午发生了什么事，怕她妻子过于罗嗦，再问下去会搞得场面尴尬，所以急忙打岔，“胡大先生在我们这里吃饭。”他说：“自己预备来不及了，我看只有叫菜来请客。”
en: “Please, please!” Watching her sway unsteadily as she brought tea herself, Hu genuinely feared she might fall. “Sister-in-Law Zhou, do not trouble yourself. You are too heavy to risk a tumble. It would be no laughing matter.” “Exactly! Do sit down,” Zhou said. “Mr Hu comes here because he treats us as his own people. All this ceremony only makes him an outsider. Let A’chun and A’qiu do whatever needs doing.” Since Hu had helped him advance, Zhou’s circumstances had steadily improved. Fond of display, he kept four servants for the elderly couple alone. A’chun and A’qiu had been bought ten years earlier and were now nearly twenty. “Better to obey than insist on ceremony.” Mrs Zhou sat down, panting, and asked after his family. “Is the old lady still strong?” “Very well, thank you.” “And Mrs Hu?” “Well enough.” She seemed about to ask after Madam Luosi and the other concubines. Zhou already knew what had happened in Hu’s household that morning. Afraid she would keep questioning him and make matters awkward, he hastily intervened. “Mr Hu will dine with us. There is no time to prepare everything ourselves. We shall have to order some dishes.”

zh: “少棠，”胡雪岩开口了：“你听我说，你不要费事！说句老实话，山珍海味我也吃厌了，尤其是这个时候，你弄好了，我也吃不下。我今天来，是想到我们从前在一起的日子，吃得落，困得着，逍遥自在，真同神仙一样，所以，此刻我不觉得自己是在做客人，你一客气，就不是我来的本意了。你懂不懂我的意思？”“本来不懂，你一说我自然就懂了。”周少棠想了一下说：“可惜，张胖子死掉了，不然邀他来一起吃‘木榔豆腐’，听他说荤笑话，哪怕外头下大雪，都不觉得冷了。”提起张胖子，胡雪岩不免伤感，怀旧之念，亦就越发炽烈，“当年的老朋友还有哪几个？”他说：“真想邀他们来叙一叙。”“这也是改天的事了。”周少棠说：“我倒想起一个人，要不要邀他来吃酒？”“哪个？”“乌先生。”
en: “Shaotang, listen. Do not put yourself to any trouble. To tell the truth, I have had my fill of rare delicacies. Especially now, I could not eat them however well you prepared them. I came because I remembered our old days together, when we could eat heartily, sleep soundly and live without a care, like immortals. I do not feel that I am a guest here. If you treat me ceremoniously, it defeats the purpose of my visit. Do you understand?” “I did not before, but now you have explained, naturally I do.” Zhou thought for a moment. “What a pity Fat Zhang is dead. Otherwise we could invite him for mulang tofu and listen to his dirty jokes. Even if it were snowing hard outside, we would not feel cold.” The mention of Fat Zhang saddened Hu and sharpened his longing for the past. “Which of our old friends are still around? I should love to gather them for a talk.” “That will have to wait for another day. But I can think of one man. Shall we invite him for a drink?” “Who?” “Mr Wu.”

zh: 胡雪岩想了一下，欣然同意：“好的、好的。”他说：“我倒又想起一个人，郑俊生。”这郑俊生是安康名家——杭州人称滩簧为“安康”，生旦净末丑，五个人坐着弹唱，而以丑为尊，称之为“小花脸”，郑俊生就是唱小花脸的。此人亦是当年与胡雪岩、周少棠一起凑份子喝酒的朋友。只为胡雪岩青云直上，身分悬殊，郑俊生自惭形秽，不愿来往，胡家有喜庆堂会，他亦从不承应。胡雪岩一想起这件事，便觉耿耿于怀，这一天很想弥补这个缺憾。周少棠知道他的心事，点点头说：“好的，我同他有来往，等我叫人去请他。”当即将他用了已经十年的佣人贵生叫了来吩咐：“你到安康郑先生家去一趟，说我请他来要有要紧事谈，回头再去请乌先生来吃酒。喔，你到了郑先生那里，千万不要说家里有客。”这是怕郑俊生知道胡雪岩在此不肯来，特意这样叮嘱。
en: After a moment, Hu gladly agreed. “Yes, yes. And I have thought of another: Zheng Junsheng.” Zheng was a celebrated performer of an’kang, the Hangzhou name for tanhuang: five seated performers sang and played the male, female, painted-face, older-male and comic roles, with the comic performer, known as the Little Painted Face, taking precedence. That was Zheng’s role. In the old days he had often pooled money with Hu and Zhou for wine. But as Hu rose swiftly in the world, the gulf between their positions had made Zheng feel inferior, and he had withdrawn. He never even accepted engagements at Hu’s household celebrations. This had always troubled Hu, and today he wanted to make amends. Understanding his feelings, Zhou nodded. “I still see him. Let me send for him.” He called Guisheng, a servant of ten years’ standing. “Go to Mr Zheng, the an’kang performer. Say I need to speak to him about something important. Then invite Mr Wu to drink with us. And when you are at Zheng’s, be sure not to mention that I have a guest.” He feared Zheng would refuse to come if he knew Hu was there.

zh: 交代完了，周少棠告个罪，又到后面跟周太太略略商量如何款客。然后在堂屋里坐定了陪胡雪岩围炉闲话。“你今天看过《申报》了？”客人先开口。“大致看了看。”周少棠说：“八个字的考语：加油添酱，胡说八道。你不要理他们。““我不在乎。你们看是骂我；我自己看，是他们捧我。”“你看得开就好。”周少棠说：“有句话，叫做‘百足之虫，死而不僵’。你只要看得开，着实还有几年快活日子过。““看得开，也不过是自己骗自己的话。这一个多月，我常常会有个怪念头，哪里去寻一种药，吃了会叫人拿过去忘记掉。”胡雪岩又说：“当然不能连自己的时辰八字、父母兄弟都忘记掉，顶好能够把日子切掉一段。”“你要切哪一段呢？”“从我认识王有龄起，到今天为止，这段日子切掉，回到我们从前在一起的辰光，那就象神仙一样了。“周少棠的心情跟他不同，觉得说回到以前过苦日子的辰光象神仙一样，未免言过其实。所以笑笑不作声。
en: After giving these instructions, Zhou excused himself and went to the back to discuss the meal briefly with his wife. Then he returned to sit with Hu by the brazier in the main hall. “Have you read Shenbao today?” his guest asked first. “Glanced through it. My verdict is simple: embroidered stories and utter nonsense. Pay no attention.” “I do not care. You see it as abuse; I see it as praise.” “As long as you can take it lightly. There is a saying: a hundred-legged insect does not fall stiff even when dead. If you can take things as they come, you still have several comfortable years ahead.” “Taking things lightly is only a way of deceiving oneself. For more than a month I have often had a strange thought: where could I find a medicine that would make me forget the past? Of course, I must not forget my own birth date and hour, my parents or my brothers. It would be best if I could cut out a stretch of my life.” “Which stretch?” “From the day I met Wang Youling until now. Cut that out and return to the days when we were together. That would be like living among immortals.” Zhou did not share his feelings. To describe a return to their former hardships as an immortal’s life seemed a considerable exaggeration. He merely smiled and said nothing.

zh: “少棠，”胡雪岩又问：“你道我现在这种境况，要做两年什么事，才会觉得做人有点乐趣？”周少棠想了好一会儿，而且是很认真地在想，但终于还是苦笑着摇摇头说：“说老实话，我想不出，只有劝你看开点。”“我自己倒想得一样。”“喔！”周少棠倒是出自衷心地想与胡雪岩同甘苦，只是身分悬殊，谈不到此，但心情是相同的，所以一听胡雪岩的话，很兴奋地催促着：“快！快说出来听听。““你不要心急，我先讲一桩事情你听。”他讲的就是在老同和的那一番奇遇。讲完了又谈他的感想：“我年年夏天施茶、施药，冬天施粥、施棉袄，另外施棺材，办育婴堂，这种好事做是在做，心里老实说一句，叫做无动于衷，所谓‘为善最乐’这句话，从没有想到过。少棠，你说，这是啥道理？”“我想！”周少棠说：“大概是因为你觉得这是你应该做的，好比每天吃饭一样，例行公事无所谓乐不乐。”“不错，发了财，就应该做这种好事，这是钱用我，不是我用钱，所以不觉得发财之可贵……”“啊，啊！我懂了。”周少棠插嘴说道：“要你想做一件事，没有钱做不成，到有了钱能够如愿，那时候才会觉得发财之可贵。”“你这话说对了一半。有钱可用，还要看机会，机会要看辰光，还要看人。”
en: “Shaotang, in my present circumstances, what could I do over the next couple of years to find some pleasure in being alive?” Zhou considered for a long time, quite earnestly, but could only shake his head with a bitter smile. “Honestly, I cannot think of anything. I can only advise you to take things less to heart.” “I have thought of something myself.” “Oh?” Zhou sincerely wished to share Hu’s fortunes, good or bad. Their unequal positions had put that beyond his reach, but the feeling was there. He urged him eagerly, “Quick, tell me!” “Do not hurry me. First let me tell you something that happened.” He related his unexpected encounter at Laotonghe, then explained what it had made him think. “Every summer I have given away tea and medicine; every winter, congee and padded coats. I have provided coffins and supported an infant foundling home. I did all these good works, yet honestly, they left my heart unmoved. The saying that doing good brings the greatest happiness never occurred to me. Why do you think that was?” “Probably because you considered it your duty. Like eating every day: a matter of routine, with no question of happiness or unhappiness.” “Exactly. A man who has made a fortune ought to do these things. That meant money was using me, instead of my using money. So I never understood the true value of being rich…” “Ah, I see!” Zhou interrupted. “You must first want to do something that lack of money prevents. When you have the money and can fulfil your wish, you appreciate its value.” “That is only half the answer. Even with money available, you must have the opportunity. That depends on the time—and on the person.”

zh: “怎么叫看人？”“譬如说，你想帮朋友的忙，无奈力不从心，忽然中了一张彩票，而那个朋友又正在为难的时候，机会岂不是很好。哪知道你把钱送了去，人家不受。这就是看人。”“为啥呢？”周少棠说：“正在需要的时候，又是好朋友，没有不受的道理。”“不受就是不受，没有道理好讲的。”“那，”周少棠不住摇头，“这个人一定多一根筋，脾气古怪，不通人情。”“换了你呢？”“换了我，一定受。”“好！”胡雪岩笑着一指，“这话是你自己说的，到时候你不要赖！”周少棠愕然，“我赖啥？”他说：“胡大先生，你的话说得我莫名其妙。”胡雪岩笑笑不答，只问：“乌先生不是住得很近吗？”原来乌先生本来住在螺蛳门外。 当年螺狮太太进胡家大门，周少棠帮忙办喜事，认识了乌先生，两人气味相投，结成至交。螺蛳太太当乌先生“娘家人”，劝他搬进城来住，有事可以就近商量。乌先生便托周少棠觅屋，在一条有名曲折的十三弯巷买的房子，两家不远，不时过从，乌太太与周太太还结拜成了姐妹。胡雪岩是因为周少棠提议邀他来喝酒，触机想起一件事，正好跟他商量，因而有此一问。
en: “What do you mean, on the person?” “Suppose you want to help a friend but cannot afford it. Suddenly you win a lottery prize, just when your friend is in trouble. Could there be a better opportunity? Yet when you take him the money, he refuses. That is what I mean.” “Why would he refuse? He needs it, and you are a good friend. There is no reason.” “Refusal is refusal. Reason has nothing to do with it.” Zhou shook his head repeatedly. “Then he must have something wrong with him—an eccentric who understands nothing of human kindness.” “What if it were you?” “I should certainly accept.” “Good!” Hu pointed at him with a smile. “Those are your own words. Do not go back on them when the time comes.” Zhou stared. “Go back on what? Mr Hu, you have completely baffled me.” Hu only smiled and asked, “Does Mr Wu not live quite nearby?” Mr Wu had originally lived outside Luosi Gate. When Madam Luosi entered Hu’s household, Zhou had helped with the wedding arrangements and met him. They had taken to each other and become close friends. Madam Luosi regarded Wu as one of her own family and urged him to move inside the city, where she could consult him more readily. He asked Zhou to find him a house and bought one in Shisanwan Lane, famous for its many turns. Their homes were close, they visited frequently, and Mrs Wu and Mrs Zhou had even become sworn sisters. Zhou’s suggestion of inviting Wu had reminded Hu of something he could discuss with him, which prompted his question.

zh: “快来了，快来了，”果不其然，不多片刻，乌先生来了，发现胡雪岩在座，顿感意外，殷勤致候，但却不便深谈。“少棠，”胡雪岩说：“我要借你的书房一用，跟乌先生说几句话。”啊唷，胡大先生，你不要笑我了，我那个记记帐的地方，哪里好叫书房？““只要有书，就是书房。”“书是有的，时宪书。”时宪书便是历本。虽然周少棠这样自嘲地说，但他的书房却还布置得并不算太俗气，又叫阿春端来一个火盆，也预备了茶，然后亲自将房门关上，好让他们从容密谈？“乌先生，我家里的事，你晓不晓得？”“啥事情？我一点都不晓得。”乌先生的神情显得有些紧张不安。“我把她们都打发走了。”“呃，”乌先生想了一下问：“几位？”“一共十个人。”胡雪岩的花园中，有名的“十二楼”，遣走十个，剩下两个，当然有螺蛳太太，此外还有一个是谁呢？
en: “He will be here soon.” Sure enough, Wu arrived before long. Surprised to find Hu there, he greeted him warmly, but it was not convenient to talk at length. “Shaotang, may I borrow your study? I should like a few words with Mr Wu.” “Oh, Mr Hu, do not make fun of me! How can my little bookkeeping room be called a study?” “Where there are books, there is a study.” “There is one book: the imperial almanac.” Despite Zhou’s self-mockery, his study was not badly furnished. He told A’chun to bring a brazier and prepare tea, then shut the door himself so that the two could speak privately at ease. “Mr Wu, do you know what has happened in my household?” “What is it? I know nothing.” Wu looked rather anxious. “I have sent them all away.” “Ah.” After a moment Wu asked, “How many?” “Ten altogether.” Hu’s garden was famous for its Twelve Chambers. Ten sent away meant two remaining. One must be Madam Luosi; who was the other?

zh: 他这样思索着尚未开口，胡雪岩却换了个话题，谈到周少棠了。“少棠的独养儿子死掉了。不孝有三，无后为大，有没有另外纳妾的意思？”何以问到这话？乌先生有些奇怪，照实答道：“我问过他，他说一时没有适当的人。”“他这两个丫头，不都大了吗？”“他都不喜欢。”乌先生说：“他太太倒有意拿阿春收房，劝过他两回，他不要。”“他要怎样的人呢？”“这很难说，不过，看样子，他倒象袁子才。”“袁子才？”胡雪岩不解，“袁子才怎么样？”“袁子才喜欢年纪大一点的，不喜欢黄毛丫头。”乌先生又念了一句诗：“徐娘风味胜雏年。”乌先生与周少棠相知甚深，据他说，在周少棠未有丧明之痛以前，贤惠得近乎滥好人的周太太，因为自己身躯臃肿不便，劝周少棠纳妾来照应起居，打算在阿春、阿秋二人中，由他挑一个来收房，周少棠便一口拒绝，原因很多。“他的话，亦不能说没有道理。”乌先生说，“老周这个人，做事不光是讲实际，而且表里兼顾，他说，他平时嘴上不大饶人，所以他要讨小纳妾，人前背后一定会有人臭他，说他得意忘形，如果讨了个不三不四，拿不出去的人，那就更加会笑他了。既然担了这样一个名声，总要真的享享艳福，才划算得来。只要人品真的好，辰光一长，笑他骂他的人，倒过来羡慕他、佩服他，那才有点意思。”
en: Before Wu could put the question, Hu changed the subject to Zhou Shaotang. “Shaotang has lost his only son. Of the three offences against filial duty, leaving no heir is the worst. Has he thought of taking a concubine?” Wondering why Hu should ask, Wu answered truthfully. “I asked him. He said he could not find a suitable woman just then.” “Are those two maids not grown up now?” “He likes neither of them. His wife wanted him to take A’chun into his chamber and urged him twice, but he refused.” “What sort of woman does he want?” “It is hard to say. But he seems rather like Yuan Zicai.” “Yuan Zicai? In what way?” “Yuan preferred women a little older, not immature young things.” Wu quoted a line: “A mature woman’s charm surpasses youthful bloom.” He knew Zhou very well. Even before their son died, Mrs Zhou, so kindhearted that she was almost indiscriminate, had urged her husband to take a concubine to look after his daily needs, since her own bulk made it difficult for her. She meant him to choose either A’chun or A’qiu, but he refused outright for several reasons. “His argument is not unreasonable,” Wu said. “He considers both practical matters and appearances. He says he is ordinarily so sharp-tongued that if he takes a concubine, people will certainly abuse him to his face and behind his back, saying prosperity has gone to his head. If he chooses some unsuitable woman he cannot present in company, they will laugh all the more. Since he must bear that reputation anyway, he should at least enjoy a real beauty. Only then is it worthwhile. If she is truly an admirable woman, the people who mock and abuse him will eventually envy and respect him instead. That would mean something.”

zh: “那么，他要怎么样的人呢？”“第一，当然是相貌，娇妻美妾，说都说死了，不美娶什么妾；第二，脾气要好，不会欺侮周太太。”胡雪岩点点头赞一声：“好！少棠总算是有良心的。”“现在情形又不同了。”乌先生接着又说：“讨小纳妾是为了传宗接代，那就再要加个第三：要宜男之相。““那么，我现在说个人，你看怎么样？我那个老七，姓朱的。”乌先生愣住了，好一会才说：“大先生，你想把七姨太，送给老周？”“是啊！”胡雪岩说：“年大将军不是做过这样的事？”“也不光是年大将军。赠妾，原是古人常有的事。不过，从你们府上出来的，眼界都高了。大先生，这件事，你还要斟酌。”“你认为哪里不妥当？”“第一，她会不会觉得委屈；第二，吃惯用惯，眼界高了，跟老周的日子过得来过不来？”“不会过不来。”胡雪岩答说：“我老实跟你说吧，我不但叫罗四姐问过她，今天早上我同她当面都提过，不会觉得委屈。再说，她到底是郎中的女儿，也知书识字，见识跟别人到底不同，跟了少棠，亦就象罗四姐跟了我一样。她也知道，我们都是为她打算。”
en: “Then what exactly does he require?” “First, looks, naturally. ‘A lovely wife and a beautiful concubine’—the saying settles it. Why take a concubine who is not beautiful? Second, a good temper: she must not bully Mrs Zhou.” Hu nodded approvingly. “Good! Shaotang has a conscience.” “Now things have changed again. The purpose of taking a concubine is to continue the family line, so a third requirement must be added: she should have the look of a woman who will bear sons.” “Then tell me what you think of someone: my seventh, the one surnamed Zhu.” Wu stared at him for a long moment. “Mr Hu, you mean to give your seventh concubine to Old Zhou?” “Why not? Did General Nian not do the same?” “Not only General Nian. Giving away concubines was common in former times. But anyone from your household will be accustomed to a great deal. Mr Hu, you should consider this carefully.” “What do you think is wrong with it?” “First, would she feel wronged? Second, with the food and comforts she is used to, could she adapt to life with Old Zhou?” “She could. To tell you the truth, I not only had Luo Sijie ask her; I spoke to her myself this morning. She will not feel wronged. Besides, she is a doctor’s daughter, educated and able to read. Her understanding is different from other women’s. With Shaotang, she would be like Luo Sijie with me. She knows we are thinking of her welfare.”

zh: “那好。不过老周呢？你同他谈过没有。”“当然谈过。”“他怎么说？”胡雪岩笑一笑说：“再好的朋友，遇到这种事，嘴上推辞，总是免不了的。”“这话我又不大敢苟同。”乌先生说：“老周这个人外圆内方，他觉得做不得的事，决不会做。”“他为啥不会做，你所说的三项条件，她都有的。”胡雪岩又说：“ 至于说朋友的姨太太，他不好意思要，这就要看旁人了，你们劝他，他会要，你们不以为然，他就答应不下。今天你同郑俊生要好好敲一敲边鼓。还有件事，我要托你，也只有你能办。”“好！大先生你说。”“要同周太太先说好。”“这！”乌先生拍拍胸脯：“包在我身上，君子成人之美，我马上就去。”“好的！不过请你私下同周太太谈，而且最好不要先告诉少棠，也不要让第三个人晓得，千万千万。”“是了！”乌先生答说：“回头我会打暗号给你。”
en: “Very well. But what about Old Zhou? Have you discussed it with him?” “Of course.” “What did he say?” Hu smiled. “However close the friendship, in a matter like this there must always be some polite refusal.” “I am not entirely convinced. Old Zhou may be accommodating on the outside, but he has firm principles within. If he thinks something wrong, he will never do it.” “Why should he refuse? She meets all three of your requirements. If he feels awkward about taking a friend’s concubine, that depends on the people around him. Encourage him and he will accept; disapprove and he will not be able to agree. You and Zheng Junsheng must give him a little encouragement today. There is something else I want to ask of you, and only you can do it.” “Please tell me.” “Settle matters with Mrs Zhou first.” Wu patted his chest. “Leave that to me. A gentleman helps bring others’ good intentions to fulfilment. I shall go at once.” “Good. But speak to her privately. It would be best not to tell Shaotang beforehand, or let anyone else know. Please be very careful.” “Understood. I shall give you a signal afterwards.”

zh: 于是一个往前，一个往后。往前的胡雪岩走到厅上，恰好遇见郑俊生进门，他从亮处望暗处，看不真切，一直上了台阶，听见胡雪岩开口招呼，方始发觉。“原来胡大先生在这里！”他在“安康”中是唱丑的，练就了插科打诨、随机应变的本事，所以稍为愣了一下，随即笑道：“怪不得今天一早起来喜鹊对我叫，遇见财神，我的运气要来了。”胡雪岩本来想说：财神倒运了。转念一想，这不等于说郑俊生运气不好，偏偏遇见正在倒媚的人？因而笑一笑改口说道：“不过财神赤脚了。”“赤脚归赤脚，财神终归是财神。”“到底是老朋友，还在捧我。”胡雪岩心中一动，他这声“财神”不应该白叫，看看有什么可以略表心意之处。正这样转着念头，只听做主人的在说：“都请坐！难得胡大先生不忘记者朋友，坐下来慢慢儿谈。”“我们先谈一谈。”郑俊生问道：“你有啥事情要夫照我，”“没有别的，专诚请你来陪胡大先生。”“喔，你挑陪客挑到我，有没有啥说法？”“是胡大先生念旧，想会会当年天天天一起的朋友。”“还有啥人？”“今天来不及了，就邀了你，还有者乌。”周少棠突然想起：“咦！老乌到哪里去了。”山来了，来了。“乌先生应声从屏风后面闪了出来，”我在后面同阿嫂谈点事，““谈好了没有？”胡雪岩问。“谈好了。”就在这一句话的交换之间，传递了信息，周少棠懵揍不觉，郑俊生更不会想到他们的话中暗藏着玄机，胡雪岩当然亦是不动声色，只在心里盘算。
en: They went in opposite directions, Hu towards the front and Wu towards the back. As Hu reached the hall, Zheng Junsheng was coming in. Looking from the light into the shade, Zheng could not see clearly; only after climbing the steps and hearing Hu greet him did he recognize him. “So Mr Hu is here!” His comic role in an’kang had trained him to improvise and turn anything into a joke. After a moment’s surprise he smiled. “No wonder the magpies called to me this morning. Meeting the God of Wealth must mean my luck is coming.” Hu was about to say that the God of Wealth had lost his luck. But would that not imply that Zheng too was unlucky, encountering a man in misfortune? He smiled and changed his answer. “Only the God of Wealth has gone barefoot.” “Barefoot or not, the God of Wealth is still the God of Wealth.” “An old friend indeed, still flattering me.” Hu felt that this title ought not to be bestowed on him for nothing. He began considering how he might show his appreciation. The host interrupted his thoughts. “Please sit down, both of you. How good of Mr Hu to remember his old friends! Let us sit and talk.” “First tell me,” Zheng asked, “what business did you want to discuss?” “Nothing except asking you here to keep Mr Hu company.” “Oh? Was there any particular reason for choosing me?” “He is thinking of old times and wanted to see friends who used to be with him every day.” “Who else is coming?” “There was no time today. I invited only you and Old Wu.” Zhou suddenly remembered. “Where has Old Wu gone?” “Here I am!” Wu emerged from behind the screen. “I was talking to Sister-in-Law in the back.” “Have you settled it?” Hu asked. “Yes.” Those few words conveyed their message. Zhou noticed nothing, and Zheng had no idea that anything lay beneath them. Hu likewise showed no outward sign, merely continuing his private calculations.

zh: “老爷！”阿春来请示：“菜都好了，是不是现在就开饭？”“客都齐了。开吧！”于是拉开桌子，摆设餐具。菜很多，有“宝饭儿”叫来的，也有自己做的，主菜是鱼头豆腐，杭州人称之为“木榔豆腐”，木榔是头的歇后语，此外有两样粗的菜，一样是肉片、豆腐衣、青菜杂烩，名为“荤素菜”，再一样，是虾油、虾子，加几粒虾仁白烧的“三虾豆腐”。这是周少棠与胡雪岩寒微之时，与朋友们凑份子吃夜饭常点的菜，由于胡雪岩念切怀旧，所以周少棠特为点了这两样菜来重温旧梦。家厨中出来的菜，讲究得多，一个硕大无朋的一品锅，是火腿煮肥鸡，另外加上二十个鸽蛋，再是一条糟蒸白鱼，光是这两样菜，加上鱼头豆腐，就将一张方桌摆满了。“请坐，胡大先生请上座。”“不！不！今天应该请乌先生首座，俊生其次，第三才是我。”“没有这个道理。”乌先生说：“我同俊生是老周这里的常客，你难得来，应该上座。”“不！乌先生，你们先坐了，我有一番道理，等下再说，说得不对，你们罚我酒，好不好。”乌先生听出一点因头来了，点点头说：“恭敬不如从命。俊生，我们两个人先坐。”坐定了斟酒，烫热了的花雕，糟香扑鼻。郑俊生贪杯，道声：“好酒！”先干了一杯，笑笑说道：“春天不是读书天，夏日炎炎正好眠，待得秋天冬已到，一杯老酒活神仙。”
en: “Master,” A’chun came to ask, “the dishes are ready. Shall we serve?” “Everyone is here. Go ahead.” The table was opened out and the places laid. There were many dishes, some ordered from Baofan’er and some cooked at home. The principal dish was fish-head tofu, called mulang tofu in Hangzhou, mulang being an allusive expression for a head. There were also two simple dishes: a mixture of sliced pork, bean-curd skin and greens, called “meat and vegetables,” and “three-shrimp tofu,” cooked in a pale sauce with shrimp oil, shrimp roe and a few shelled shrimps. These were dishes Hu and Zhou had often ordered when pooling their money with friends for an evening meal in their poor days. Since Hu longed so deeply for the past, Zhou had ordered them specially to revive those memories. The home-cooked dishes were far more elaborate. An enormous yipin pot held a fat chicken cooked with ham, with twenty pigeon eggs added. There was also a whitefish steamed with wine lees. Those two dishes and the fish-head tofu alone filled the square table. “Please, Mr Hu, take the seat of honour.” “No, no. Today Mr Wu should sit first, Junsheng next, and I third.” “That cannot be right,” Wu said. “Junsheng and I are regular visitors here. You seldom come. The place of honour is yours.” “Please sit first. I have my reasons and shall explain them later. If they are wrong, you may make me drink a penalty cup. Will that do?” Wu caught a hint and nodded. “Better to obey than insist on ceremony. Junsheng, let us sit.” Once they were seated, wine was poured. The warmed Huadiao gave off a rich fermented fragrance. Fond of his drink, Zheng exclaimed, “Excellent wine!” He drained a cup and recited with a smile: “Spring is no season for studying books; summer’s heat is best for sleep. By the time autumn comes, winter is here—a cup of old wine makes an immortal of me.”

zh: 大家都笑了，胡雪岩便说：“俊生，你今天要好好儿唱一段给我听听。”“一句话，你喜欢听啥？可惜没有带只三弦来，只有干唱了。”“你的拿手活儿是‘马浪荡，，说多于唱，没有三弦也不要紧。”“三弦家伙我有地方借，不要紧！”周少棠高高举杯，“来、来，酒菜都要趁热。”有的浅尝一口，有的一吸而尽，郑俊生于了杯还照一照，口中说道：“说实话，我实在没有想到，今天会在这里同胡大先生一淘吃酒。”这句话听起来有笑胡雪岩“落魄”的意味，作主人的周少棠，为了冲淡可能会发生的误会，接口说道：“我也没有想到胡大先生今天会光降，难得的机会，不醉无归。”“难得老朋友聚会，我有一句心里话要说。”胡雪岩停了下来，视线扫了一周，最后落在郑俊生身上：“俊生，你这一向怎么样？”郑俊生不知他问这句话的用意，想一想答说：“还不是老样子，吃不饱、饿不杀。”“你要怎样才吃得饱？”从来没有人问过他这话，他自己也没有想过这一点。他愣了一下，忽然想到曾一度想过、而自以为是胡思乱想、旋即丢开的念头，随即说出口来。“我自己能弄它一个班子就好了。”
en: They all laughed. “Junsheng, you must perform something for me today,” Hu said. “Only say what you want to hear. A pity I did not bring a sanxian; I shall have to sing without accompaniment.” “Your speciality is Ma the Rake, and there is more talking than singing in that. The sanxian will hardly matter.” “I know where to borrow one. No difficulty!” Zhou raised his cup high. “Come, come. Wine and food should both be taken hot.” Some sipped; others drained their cups. Zheng finished his and displayed the empty bottom. “To tell the truth, I never expected to be drinking here with Mr Hu today.” It could sound as though he were mocking Hu’s fall. To dispel any possible misunderstanding, Zhou quickly said, “Nor did I expect the honour of his visit. Such a rare gathering deserves a proper drinking session. Nobody goes home sober.” “Since old friends have so seldom met, there is something I want to say from the heart.” Hu paused, looked round and let his gaze settle on Zheng. “Junsheng, how have things been with you lately?” Unsure what lay behind the question, Zheng thought, then answered, “Much as always. Never enough to fill me, never so little as to starve.” “What would it take to fill you?” Nobody had ever asked him that, and he had never considered it himself. He hesitated. Then he remembered an idea he had once entertained and immediately dismissed as a foolish dream. He spoke it aloud. “If only I could start a troupe of my own.”

zh: “喔，”胡雪岩紧接着问：“怎么个弄法？”“有钱马上就弄起来了。”“你说！”这一来，周少棠与乌先生部知道胡雪岩的用意了，一起用眼色怂恿郑俊生快说。郑俊生当然也明白了，胡雪岩有资助他的意思，心里不免踌躇，因为一直不愿向胡雪岩求助，而当他事业失败之时，反而出此一举，自然是件不合情理之事。“你说啊！”周少棠催他：“你自己说的，胡大先生虽然赤脚，到底是财神，帮你千把银子弄个班子起来的忙，还是不费吹灰之力。”“却之下恭，受之有愧。而且自己觉得有点于心不甘。此话怎讲？”郑俊生自问自答地说：“想想应该老早跟胡大先生开口的，那就不止一千两银子了。不过，”他特别提高了声音，下个转语：“我要早开口，胡大先生作兴上万银子帮我，那是锦上添花，不如现在雪中送炭的一千两银子，情意更重。”周少棠听他的话，先是一愣，然后发笑，“熟透了的两句成语，锦上添花，雪中送炭，你这样拿来用，倒也新鲜。”“不过，”乌先生接口道：“细细想一想，他也并没有用错，胡大先生自己在雪地里，还要为人家送炭，自然更加难得，来、来，干一杯，但愿俊生的班子，有一番轰轰烈烈的作为。”“谢谢金口。”郑俊生喝干了酒，很兴奋地说：“我这个班子，要就不成功，要成功了的话，你们各位看在那里好了，一定都是一等一的好角色。”“不错！我也是这样子在想，凡事要么不做，要做就要象个样子。俊生，你放手去干，钱，不必发愁，三五千银子，我还凑得出来。”
en: “Oh? How would you go about it?” “With money, I could start at once.” “Tell me.” By now Zhou and Wu both understood Hu’s intention. They urged Zheng on with their eyes. Zheng understood too: Hu meant to help finance him. Yet he hesitated. He had always refused to ask Hu for assistance. To do so now, after Hu’s business had failed, would hardly be reasonable. “Go on!” Zhou urged. “You said it yourself: Mr Hu may be barefoot, but he is still the God of Wealth. Helping you with a thousand taels or so to start a troupe would be no effort at all.” “To refuse would be disrespectful; to accept leaves me ashamed. And I feel a little regret besides. Why? I ought to have spoken to Mr Hu long ago. Then it would have been more than a thousand taels. But”—Zheng raised his voice to make his turn—“had I asked earlier, he might have given me ten thousand. That would have been flowers added to brocade. A thousand now is charcoal brought through snow, and the kindness is greater.” Zhou stared, then laughed. “Two expressions everybody knows—flowers on brocade and charcoal in snow. You have found a novel way of using them.” “Yet, when one thinks about it, he has not used them wrongly,” Wu said. “Mr Hu is himself out in the snow and still brings charcoal to others. That makes it all the more remarkable. Come, let us drink, and wish Junsheng’s troupe a splendid future.” “Thank you for those auspicious words.” Zheng drained his cup and said excitedly, “Either this troupe will come to nothing, or, if it succeeds, you will see: every performer will be first-rate.” “Exactly what I think. Either do not undertake something, or do it properly. Junsheng, go ahead without hesitation. Do not worry about money. I can still raise three or five thousand taels.”

zh: 郑俊生点点头，双眼乱眨着，似乎心中别有盘算。就这时，阿秋走来，悄悄在周少棠耳际说了句，“太太请，”“啥事情？”“不晓得，只说请者爷抽个空进去，太太有话说。”“好！”周少棠站起身来说：“暂且失陪。我去去就来。”等他一走，郑俊生欲言又止，踌躇了一会，方始开口，但却先向乌先生使个眼色，示意他细听。“胡大先生，我有个主意，你算出本钱，让我去立个班子，一切从宽计算，充其量两千银子。不过你要给我五千，另外三千备而不用。”说着，他又抛给乌先生一个眼色，“这回是示意他搭腔。乌先生是极细心、极能体会世情的人，知道郑俊生的用意，这三千银子，胡雪岩随时可以收回，亦隐隐然有代为寄顿之意——中国的刑律，自有”籍没“，亦就是俗语所说的抄家这一条以来，便有寄顿资财于至亲好友之家的办法，但往往由于受托是犯法的行为，受托者每有难色；至于自告奋勇、愿意受寄者，百不得一。乌先生相信郑俊生是见义勇为，决无趁火打劫之意，但对胡雪岩来说，这数目太小了，不值一谈，所以乌先生佯作不知，默然无语。其实，郑俊生倒确是一番为胡雪岩着想的深刻用心，他是往最坏的方面去想，设想胡雪岩在革职以后会抄家，一家生活无着，那时候除了这三千两银子以外，还有由他的资本而设置的一个班子，所人亦可维生，郑俊生本人只愿以受雇的身分，领取一份薪水而已。胡雪岩自是全然想不到此，只很爽快地答应：“好！我借你五千银子。只要人家说一声：听滩簧一定要郑俊生的班子。我这五千银子就很值了。“胡雪岩接着又对乌先生说：“你明天到我这里来一趟，除了俊生这件事以外，我另外还有话同你说。”
en: Zheng nodded, blinking rapidly, as though some other calculation occupied him. Just then A’qiu came and whispered in Zhou’s ear, “Madam would like to see you.” “What about?” “I do not know. She only asks you to spare a moment. She has something to say.” “Very well.” Zhou stood. “Excuse me. I shall be back shortly.” Once he had gone, Zheng seemed about to speak, then stopped. After hesitating, he finally began, first giving Wu a look that asked him to listen carefully. “Mr Hu, I have an idea. You provide the capital, and I shall start a troupe. Even allowing generously for everything, two thousand taels would be the most it could cost. But give me five thousand. I shall keep the other three thousand in reserve.” He cast Wu another glance, inviting him to join in. Wu was observant and understood the ways of the world. He recognized the purpose: Hu could reclaim the three thousand at any time. It also hinted at keeping money safe for him. Ever since confiscation had entered Chinese criminal law, people had placed property with close relatives and friends to preserve it. But accepting such property was itself an offence, so those asked often hesitated. Fewer than one in a hundred volunteered. Wu believed Zheng was acting courageously out of friendship, with no intention of profiting from Hu’s distress. To Hu, however, the sum would be too small to discuss. Wu therefore pretended not to understand and remained silent. Zheng’s concern was in fact far-reaching. Imagining the worst, he feared that dismissal would be followed by confiscation, leaving Hu’s family without a livelihood. Then, besides the three thousand taels, there would be a troupe established with Hu’s capital, whose earnings could support them. Zheng himself would be content to draw a salary as an employee. None of this occurred to Hu. He readily agreed. “Good. I shall lend you five thousand. If people say, ‘For tanhuang, you must hear Zheng Junsheng’s troupe,’ my five thousand will have been well spent.” Turning to Wu, he added, “Come to my house tomorrow. Besides Junsheng’s business, there is something else I want to discuss.”

zh: 谈到这里，只见周少棠去而复回，入席以后亦不讲话，只是举怀相劝，而他自己却有些心不在焉的模样，引杯及唇，却又放下，一双筷子宕在半空中，仿佛不知从何下著。这种情形，胡雪岩、乌先生看在眼里，相视微笑，郑俊生却莫名其妙。“怎么搞的？”他问：“神魂颠倒，好象有心事。”“是有心事，从来没有过的。”周少棠看着胡雪岩说：“胡大先生，你叫我怎么说？”原来刚才周太太派丫头将周少棠请了进去，就是谈胡雪岩赠妾之事。周太太实在很贤惠，乐见这一桩好事，虽然乌先生照胡雪岩的意思，关照她先不必告诉周少棠，但她怕周少棠不明了她的心意，人家一提这桩好事，他一定会用“我要先问问内人的意思”的话来回答。那一来徒费周折，不知直截了当先表朋态度。在周少棠有此意外的姻缘，自然喜不自胜，但就做朋友的道理来说，少不得要惺惺作态一番。这时候就要旁人来敲边鼓了，乌先生在胡雪岩的眼色授意之下，便向郑俊生说道：“我们要吃老周的喜酒了。”“喔，喔，好啊！”郑俊生见多识广，看到周少棠与胡雪岩之间那种微妙的神情，已有所觉，“大概是胡大先生府上的哪个大姐，要变成周家姨太太了。”“大姐”是指丫头，乌先生答说：“你猜到了一半，不是赠婢是赠妾。我们杭州，前有年大将军，后有胡大先生。“接着便将经过情形说了一遍，大大地将朱姨太太夸赞了一番。“恭喜，恭喜！又是一桩西湖佳话。”郑俊生说：“谈到年大将军，他当初拿姨太太送人是有用意的，不比胡大先生一方面是为了朋友传宗接代，一方面是为了姨太太有个好归宿，光明正大，义气逼人。这桩好事，要把官维持到底，照我看，要有个做法。”
en: Zhou returned and resumed his seat without speaking, merely raising his cup to his guests. He seemed distracted: his cup reached his lips and was set down again; his chopsticks hovered in the air as though he could not decide where to begin. Hu and Wu exchanged knowing smiles. Zheng was puzzled. “What has happened? You seem quite bewildered, as though something were on your mind.” “There is—something quite unprecedented.” Zhou looked at Hu. “Mr Hu, what am I to say?” Mrs Zhou had summoned him to discuss Hu’s gift of a concubine. She was truly a considerate wife and delighted at the prospect. Although Wu, following Hu’s instructions, had asked her not to tell Zhou beforehand, she feared that her husband, uncertain of her feelings, would answer any proposal with, “I must consult my wife first.” That would only create needless complications. Better to make her position clear at once. Zhou was naturally overjoyed by this unexpected marriage, but friendship required a show of reluctance. Now someone else must encourage him. At a glance from Hu, Wu told Zheng, “We shall be drinking at Old Zhou’s wedding.” “Oh, excellent!” Experienced in the world, Zheng had noticed the subtle expressions passing between Zhou and Hu and guessed something of the truth. “One of the young ladies in Mr Hu’s household is to become a concubine in the Zhou family, I suppose?” By “young ladies” he meant maids. “You are half right,” Wu answered. “It is a concubine being given, not a maid. Hangzhou had General Nian in the past; now it has Mr Hu.” He explained the circumstances and praised Mistress Zhu warmly. “Congratulations! Another fine West Lake story,” Zheng said. “But General Nian had a purpose when he gave away concubines. Mr Hu wants both to continue a friend’s family line and to find a good home for the woman. It is an open, honourable act of extraordinary generosity. To keep this a good thing to the end, however, I think there is a precaution we should take.”

zh: “喔，”胡雪岩很注意地问：“请你说，要怎么做？”“我先说当初年大将军，拿姨太太送人，也不止在杭州的一个，而且他送人的姨太太，都是有孕在身的……”原来年羹尧的祖先本姓严，安徽怀远人，始祖名叫严富，两榜及第中了进士，写榜时，误严为年。照定例是可以请求礼部更正的，但那一来便须办妥一切手续后，方能分发任官，未免耽误前程，因而将错就错，改用榜名年富。年富入仕后，被派到辽东当巡按御史，子孙便落籍在那里。及至清太祖起兵，辽东的汉人，被俘为奴，称为“包衣”。包衣有“上三旗”、“下五旗”之分，上三旗的包衣隶属内务府，下五旗的包衣则分隶诸王门下。年羹尧的父亲年遐龄、长兄年希尧及他本人，在康熙朝皆为雍亲王门下，雍亲王便是后来的雍正皇帝，年羹尧的妹妹，原是雍亲王的侧福晋，以后封为贵妃。包衣从龙入关后，一样也能参加考试，而且因为有亲贵奥援，飞黄腾达，往往是指顾间事。
en: “Please explain. What should we do?” Hu asked attentively. “First let me tell you that General Nian gave away more than one concubine, and not only in Hangzhou. Every woman he gave away was pregnant…” In Zheng’s account, Nian Gengyao’s ancestors had originally borne the surname Yan and came from Huaiyuan in Anhui. The founder of the line was Yan Fu, who passed the examinations and became a jinshi. When the list of successful candidates was written, his surname Yan was mistakenly written as Nian. Under the regulations he could have requested a correction from the Ministry of Rites, but all the formalities would have had to be completed before he could receive an appointment. Rather than delay his career, he accepted the error and used the name Nian Fu. On entering office he was sent to Liaodong as inspecting censor, and his descendants settled there. When the Qing founder Taizu took up arms, the Han Chinese of Liaodong were captured and made bondservants, called booi. They were divided between the Upper Three and the Lower Five Banners. Those of the Upper Three came under the Imperial Household Department; those of the Lower Five served the princes. During the Kangxi reign, Nian Gengyao’s father Nian Xialing, his elder brother Nian Xiyao and Nian Gengyao himself all belonged to the household of Prince Yong, the future Yongzheng Emperor. Nian Gengyao’s younger sister had been the prince’s secondary consort and later became a Noble Consort. After following their rulers through the passes into China, bondservants could also sit the examinations. With powerful imperial relatives to support them, advancement could come in the twinkling of an eye.

zh: 年遐龄官至湖广巡抚，年希尧亦是二品大员，年羹尧本人是康熙三十九年的翰林，由于雍亲王的推荐，出任四川总督。其实，这是雍亲王为了夺嫡布下的一着棋。原一为康熙晚年已经选定了皇位继承人，即是雍亲王的同母弟、皇十四子恂郡王胤祯，当他奉命以大将军出征青海时，特许使用正黄旗县，暗示代替天子亲征，亦即暗示天命有归。恂郡玉将成为未来的皇帝，是一个心照不宣的公开秘密。询郡王征青海的主动助手便是年羹尧。及至康熙六十一年冬天，皇帝得病，势将不起，急召恂郡王来京时，却为手握重兵的年羹尧所钳制，因此，雍亲王得以勾结康熙皇帝的亲信、后来为雍正尊称为“舅舅”的隆科多，巧妙地夺得了皇位。雍正的城府极深，在夺位不久，便决定要杀隆科多与年羹尧灭口。因此，起初对年羹尧甘言蜜语，笼络备至，养成他的骄恣之气。年羹尧本来就很跋扈，自以为皇帝有把柄在他手里，无奈其何，越发起了不臣之心，种种作为都显出他是吴三桂第二。但时势不同，吴三桂尚且失败，年羹尧岂有幸理。雍正用翦除他的羽翼以及架空他的兵权的手法，双管齐下，到他乞饶不允，年羹尧始知有灭门之祸，因而以有孕之妾赠人，希望留下自己的骨血。
en: Nian Xialing rose to be governor of Huguang; Nian Xiyao too became a senior official of the second rank. Nian Gengyao entered the Hanlin Academy in the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi. Recommended by Prince Yong, he became governor-general of Sichuan. This was actually a move in the prince’s struggle for the succession. In his later years, Kangxi had already chosen an heir: Prince Yong’s full brother, the fourteenth imperial son Yinzhen, Prince Xun. When ordered to campaign in Qinghai as commander-in-chief, he was specially permitted to use the Plain Yellow Banner, implying that he represented the emperor on campaign and that Heaven’s mandate would pass to him. His future accession was an open secret. Nian Gengyao was his chief support in the Qinghai campaign. In the winter of Kangxi’s sixty-first year, the emperor fell gravely ill and urgently summoned Prince Xun to the capital, but Nian, commanding powerful forces, held him back. Prince Yong was thus able to collude with Kangxi’s confidant Longkodo, whom he later honoured as “Uncle,” and skilfully seize the throne. Yongzheng concealed his intentions deeply. Soon after taking power, he decided to kill both Longkodo and Nian to silence them. At first he flattered Nian and showed him every favour, encouraging his arrogance. Already overbearing, Nian believed he held the emperor’s secret and was therefore untouchable. His disloyal ambitions grew until his conduct resembled that of a second Wu Sangui. But circumstances had changed. Even Wu Sangui had failed; what hope had Nian? Yongzheng simultaneously stripped away his supporters and emptied his military authority of substance. Only when his pleas for mercy were refused did Nian realize that his whole family faced destruction. He therefore gave away pregnant concubines in the hope of preserving his own bloodline.

zh: 郑俊生的这番话，在座的人都是闻所未闻，“那么，”乌先生问：“年羹尧有没有留下亲骨血呢？”“有。”郑俊生答说：“有个怪姓，就是我郑俊生的生字。凡姓生的，就是年羹尧的后代。”“为什么要取这么一个怪姓。”“这也是有来历的，年字倒过来，把头一笔的一撇移到上面，看起来不就象生字？”郑俊生说：“闲话表过，言归正传。我是想到，万一朱姨太太有孕在身，将来两家乱了血胤，不大好。”“啊，啊！”乌先生看着胡雪岩说：“这要问大先生自己了。”“这也难说得很。”胡雪岩沉吟了一会说：“老郑的话很不错，本来是一桩好事，将来弄出误会来倒不好了，为了保险起见，我倒有个办法，事情我们就说定了。请少棠先找一处地方，让她一个人住两个月，看她一切如常再圆房。你们看好不好？”“对，对！”郑俊主与乌先生不约而同地表示赞成。“那么，两位就算媒人。怎么样安排，还要请两位费心。
en: None of those present had heard this account before. “Then did Nian leave any descendants?” Wu asked. “Yes. There is an unusual surname, Sheng—the last character of my own name, Zheng Junsheng. Everyone surnamed Sheng is descended from Nian Gengyao.” “Why choose such an odd surname?” “There is a story behind that too. Turn the character Nian upside down and move its first slanting stroke to the top. Does it not look like Sheng?” Zheng continued, “But enough of the digression. Back to our business. Suppose Mistress Zhu is already pregnant. If the bloodlines of the two families become confused, that will be unfortunate.” “Ah!” Wu looked at Hu. “We must ask Mr Hu about that.” “It is hard to be certain.” Hu thought for a while. “Old Zheng has a point. What begins as a good thing should not lead to misunderstanding. To be safe, I have a plan. Let us settle the match now. Shaotang can first find a place where she can live alone for two months. Once it is clear that everything is normal, they can consummate the marriage. What do you think?” “Yes, yes!” Zheng and Wu agreed together. “Then you two shall be the matchmakers. I must trouble you to see to the arrangements.”

zh: 原来请乌先生跟郑俊生上坐的缘故在此。事到如今，周少棠亦就老老脸皮，不再说假惺惺的话，逐一敬酒，头一个敬胡雪岩。“胡大先生，我什么话都用不着说，总而言之，路遥知马力，日久见人心。倘若我能不绝后，我们周家的祖宗，在阴世都会给胡大先生你磕头。”“失言，失言！”胡雪岩说：“你怎么好说这样的话，罚酒。”“是，是，罚酒。”周少棠干了第二杯酒以后，又举杯敬乌先生。“应该先敬他。”乌先生指着郑俊生说：“不是他看得透，说不定弄出误会来，蛮好的一桩事情。变得糟不可言，那就叫人哭不出来了。”“不错！”胡雪岩接口，“提到这一层，我都要敬一敬老郑。”“不敢当，不敢当。”三个人都干了酒，最后轮到乌先生。“老周，”他自告奋勇，“你的喜事，我来替你提调。”“那就再好都没有。拜托拜托！”这一顿酒，第一个醉的是主人，胡雪岩酒量不佳，不敢多喝，清醒如常，散席后邀乌先生到家里作长夜之谈。乌先生欣然同意。两人辞谢主人，又与郑俊生作别，带着小厮安步回元宝街。
en: So that was why Hu had insisted that Wu and Zheng take the places of honour. Matters had gone this far; Zhou now put aside embarrassment and empty protestations. He offered toasts to each in turn, beginning with Hu. “Mr Hu, there is nothing I need say. Distance tests a horse’s strength; time reveals a person’s heart. If my family line can be preserved, all our Zhou ancestors in the other world will kowtow to you.” “A slip of the tongue!” Hu said. “How can you say such a thing? Drink a penalty.” “Yes, a penalty.” After finishing a second cup, Zhou raised another to Wu. “You should toast him first.” Wu pointed at Zheng. “Without his foresight, there might have been a misunderstanding that turned a fine affair into a dreadful mess. We should have been beyond tears.” “Quite right,” Hu said. “For that thought, I must drink to Old Zheng myself.” “You are too kind.” All three drained their cups. Finally it was Wu’s turn. “Old Zhou, let me manage the wedding for you.” “Nothing could be better. I leave it in your hands.” The host was the first to become drunk. Hu, who had little capacity for wine, drank cautiously and remained as clearheaded as ever. When the meal ended, he invited Wu home for a long night’s conversation. Wu gladly agreed. They thanked their host, said goodbye to Zheng, and set off on foot for Yuanbao Street with the servant.

zh: 走到半路，发现迎面来了一乘轿子，前后两盏灯笼，既大且亮。胡雪岩一看就知道了，拉一拉乌先生，站在石板路正中不动。走近了一看，果然不错，大灯笼上，扁宋字一面是“庆余堂”，一面是个“胡”字。问起来才知道螺蛳太太不放心，特意打发轿子来接。但主客二人，轿只一乘，好在家也近了，胡雪岩吩咐空轿抬回，他仍旧与乌先生步行而归。一进了元宝街，颇有陌生的感觉，平时如果夜归，自街口至大门，都有灯笼照明，这天漆黑一片，遥遥望去，一星灯火，只是角门上点着一盏灯笼。但最凄凉的却是花园里，楼台十二，暗影沉沉，只有百狮楼中，灯火通明，却反而显得凄清。因为相形之下，格外容易使人兴起人去楼空的沧桑之感。这时阿云已经迎了上来，一见前有客人，定睛细看了一下，惊讶地说：“原来是乌先生。”“乌先生今天住在这里。”胡雪岩说，“你去告诉螺蛳太太。阿云答应着，返身而去。等他们上了百狮楼，螺蛳太太已亲自打开门帘在等，一见乌先生，不知如何，悲从中来，眼泪忍不住夺眶而出，赶紧背过身去，拭一拭眼泪，再回过身来招呼。“请用茶！”螺蛳太太亲自来招待乌先生。“不敢当，谢谢！”乌先生看她神情憔悴，不免关心，“罗四姐，”他说，“你现在责任更加重了，千万要自己保重。”“唉！”螺蛳太太微喟着，“真象一场梦。”“嘘！”乌先生双指撮唇，示意她别说这些颓丧的话。
en: Halfway home they saw a sedan chair approaching, preceded and followed by two large, bright lanterns. Hu recognized it at once. He tugged Wu’s sleeve and stopped in the middle of the stone-paved road. As it drew nearer, he saw that he was right: each large lantern bore “Qingyu Hall” on one side and “Hu” on the other, in broad, flattened Song-style lettering. On inquiry, he learned that Madam Luosi, worried about him, had sent the chair to fetch him. But there were two men and only one chair. Since they were close to home, he ordered it carried back empty and continued walking with Wu. Yuanbao Street felt strangely unfamiliar. Ordinarily, when he returned at night, lanterns lit the whole way from the street entrance to his gate. Tonight it was black. In the distance only a single lantern burned at the side gate. Most desolate of all was the garden. Its twelve towers and pavilions stood in dark shadow. Hundred Lions Tower alone was brightly lit, yet its light made the scene seem lonelier, sharpening the sense of a world changed, its people gone and buildings empty. A’yun came to meet them. Noticing the guest, she looked closely. “Why, it is Mr Wu!” “Mr Wu will stay here tonight. Tell Madam Luosi.” She hurried back. By the time they reached Hundred Lions Tower, Madam Luosi herself was holding the door curtain aside. For some reason, the sight of Wu suddenly overwhelmed her with grief. Tears sprang from her eyes. She turned away, wiped them quickly, and turned back to greet him. “Please have some tea.” She attended to him herself. “You are too kind. Thank you.” Seeing how worn she looked, Wu was concerned. “Luo Sijie, your responsibilities are greater than ever now. You must take care of yourself.” “Ah!” she sighed. “It really is like a dream.” Wu raised two fingers to his lips, warning her away from such dispiriting talk.

zh: “听说你们是走回来的？这么大的西北风，脸都冻红了。”螺蛳太太喊道：“阿云，赶快打洗脸水来！”“脸上倒还不太冷，脚冻僵了。”螺蛳太太回头看了一眼，见胡雪岩与阿云在说话，便即轻声问道：“今天的事，你晓得了？”“听说了。”“你看这样做，对不对呢？”“对！提得起，放得下，应该这么做。”“提得起，放不下，今天是提不动，不得不放手。”螺蛳太太说：“乌先生，换了你，服不服这口气？”“不服又怎么样？”胡雪岩在另一方面接口。乌先生不作声。螺蛳太太停了一下才说：“我是不服这口气。等一下，好好儿商量商量。“她又问道：”乌先生饿不饿？““不饿，不饿。“不饿就先吃酒，再开点心。”螺蛳太太回身跟胡雪岩商量：“乌先生就住楼下书房好了？”“好！”胡雪岩说：“索性请乌先生到书房里去吃酒谈天。”这表示胡雪岩与乌先生要作长夜之谈。螺蛳太太答应着，带了阿云下楼去安排。乌先生看在眼里，不免感触，更觉关切，心里有个一直盘桓着的疑团，急于打破。
en: “I hear you walked back. With that fierce northwesterly wind, your faces are red with cold.” Madam Luosi called, “A’yun, bring hot water for them to wash!” “My face is not too cold, but my feet are frozen.” Glancing back, she saw Hu talking to A’yun and lowered her voice. “Have you heard about today?” “Yes.” “Do you think we did right?” “Yes. If one can take something up, one must be able to put it down. It was the right thing.” “He could take it up, but could not put it down. Today he had to let go because he could no longer carry it. Mr Wu, if it were you, could you accept such a defeat?” “What good would refusing to accept it do?” Hu put in from the other side of the room. Wu said nothing. After a pause, Madam Luosi answered, “I will not accept it. We must discuss it properly later.” She asked Wu, “Are you hungry?” “No, not at all.” “Then wine first, and refreshments afterwards.” Turning to Hu, she asked, “Shall Mr Wu sleep in the downstairs study?” “Yes. Let us go down there to drink and talk.” This meant that their conversation would last well into the night. Madam Luosi agreed and took A’yun downstairs to make arrangements. Watching her, Wu felt more deeply moved and concerned. A question that had long troubled him now demanded an answer.

zh: “大先生，”他说：“我现在说句老话：无官一身轻。你往后作何打算？”“你的话只说对了一半，‘无官’不错，‘一身轻’则不见得。”“不轻要想法子来轻。”他问：“左大人莫非就不帮你的忙？”“他现在的力量也有限了。”胡雪岩说：“应春到南京去了。等他来了，看是怎么个说法？”乌先生沉吟了好一会，终于很吃力地说了出来：“朝廷还会有什么处置？会不会查抄？““只要公款还清，就不会查抄。”胡雪岩又说：“公款有查封的典当作抵，慢慢儿还，我可以不管，就是私人的存款，将来不知道能打几折来还。一想到这一层，我的肩膀上就象有副千斤重担，压得我直不起腰来。““其实，这是你心里不轻，不是身上不轻。你能不能看开一点呢？”“怎么个看开法？”“不去想它，”胡雪岩笑笑不作声，然后顾左右而言他地说，“乌先生，你不要忘记少棠的事，回头同罗四姐好好谈一谈。”“唉！”乌先生摇摇头，“你到这时候，还只想到人家的闲事。”“只有这样子，我才会不想我自己的事。我自己的事管不了，只好管人家的闲事，管好人家的闲事，心里有点安慰，其实也就是管我自己的事。”“这就是为善最乐的道理。可惜，今年……”
en: “Mr Hu, let me repeat an old saying: without office, a man is free of burdens. What are your plans?” “You are only half right. Without office, yes; free of burdens, scarcely.” “Then we must find a way to lighten them. Will Lord Zuo not help?” “His powers are limited now too. Yingchun has gone to Nanjing. We shall see what he has to say when he returns.” Wu pondered for a long time before he could bring himself to ask, “What further action will the court take? Will your property be confiscated?” “Not if the public debts are repaid. The pawnshops taken into official custody can be set against them and repay them gradually. I need not concern myself with those. It is the private deposits: I do not know what proportion I shall eventually be able to repay. Whenever I think of that, it is like a thousand-jin burden on my shoulders, bending me double.” “Then it is your heart that is burdened, rather than your person. Can you not take things more lightly?” “How?” “Stop thinking about them.” Hu smiled without answering and changed the subject. “Mr Wu, do not forget Shaotang’s business. Discuss it properly with Luo Sijie later.” Wu shook his head. “Even now, you think only of other people’s private affairs.” “Only that lets me stop thinking about my own. I cannot manage my affairs, so I occupy myself with other people’s. If I manage theirs well, it gives me some comfort. In that sense I am attending to my own affairs too.” “That is the meaning of finding happiness in doing good. A pity that this year…”

zh: “我懂，我懂！”胡雪岩接口说道：“我亦正要同你商量这件事。今天去看少棠，去也是走路去的，西北风吹在脸上发痛，我心里就在想，身上狐皮袍子，头上戴的是貂帽，脚下棉鞋虽是旧的，不过鞋底上黑少白多，也同薪的一样。这样子的穿戴还觉得冷，连件棉袄都没有的人，怎么样过冬？我去上海之前，老太太还从山上带口信下来，说今年施棉衣、施粥，应该照常。不过，乌先生，你说，我现在的情形，怎么样还好做好事？““我说可惜，也就是为此。你做这种好事的力量，还是有的，不过那一来，一定会有人说闲话说得很难听。”乌先生叹口气：“现在我才明白，做好事都要看机会的。”“一点不错。？胡雪岩说：”刚才同你走回来，身上一冷，我又想到了这件事。这桩好事，还是不能不做。你看有什么办法？““你不能出面，你出面一定会挨骂，而且对清理都有影响”对！“胡雪岩说：”我想请你来出面。“”人家不相信的。“乌先生不断摇头：”我算老几，哪里有施棉衣、施粥的资格。“正在筹无善策时。螺蛳太太派阿云上来通知，书房里部署好了，请主客二人下楼用消夜。
en: “I understand. That is exactly what I wanted to discuss.” Hu continued, “I walked to Shaotang’s today, and the northwesterly wind stung my face. I thought: here I am in a fox-fur robe and a sable cap. My padded shoes may be old, but their soles show more white than black and are as good as new. If I am cold dressed like this, how will people without even a padded coat survive the winter? Before I went to Shanghai, my mother sent word down from the hills that this year’s distribution of padded clothing and congee should continue as usual. But in my present circumstances, how can I still do charitable work?” “That is what I meant by a pity. You still have the means, but if you do it, people are certain to say very ugly things.” Wu sighed. “Only now do I understand that even doing good requires the right opportunity.” “Exactly. Walking back with you, the cold made me think of it again. This good work must still be done. Can you see a way?” “You cannot appear in it yourself. If you do, people will abuse you, and it will even affect the settlement of your debts.” “Precisely. I was thinking of asking you to appear for me.” Wu shook his head repeatedly. “Nobody would believe it. Who am I? What standing have I to distribute padded clothing and congee?” While they were unable to find an answer, A’yun came upstairs at Madam Luosi’s direction. Everything was ready in the study; host and guest were invited down for supper.

zh: 消夜亦很丰盛，明灯璀璨，炉火熊熊。乌先生知道象这样作客的日子也不多了，格外珍惜，所以暂抛愁怀，且享受眼前，浅斟低酌，细细最尝满桌子的名酒美食。直到第二壶花雕烫上来时，他才开口：“大先生，我倒想到一个法子，不如你用无名氏的名义。捐一笔款子，指定用途，也一样的。”话一出口，螺蛳太太插嘴问说。“你们在谈啥？”“谈老太太交代的那件事。”胡雪岩略略说了经过。“那么，你预备捐多少呢？”“你看呢？”胡雪岩反问。“往年冬天施棉衣，施粥，总要用到三万银子。现在力量不够了。我看顶多捐一万人。”“好！”胡雪岩点点头说：“这个数目酌乎其中，就是一万。”“这一万银子，请乌先生拿去捐。不过，虽说无名氏，总还是有人晓得真正的名字。我看，要说是老太太捐的私房钱。你根本不晓得；要这样说法，你的脚步才站得住。”胡雪岩与乌先生都深以为然。时入隆冬，这件好事要做得不能有片刻延误，为此，螺蛳太太特为离席上楼去筹划——她梳妆台中有一本帐，是这天从各房姨太太处检查出来的私房，有珠宝、也有金银，看看能不能凑出一万银子？
en: Supper was plentiful, the lamps shone brilliantly, and the fire blazed. Wu knew that few evenings as a guest in such surroundings remained to him. He treasured this one all the more, putting aside his worries to enjoy the moment, sipping slowly and savouring the fine wine and food. Only when the second pot of Huadiao was warmed did he speak. “Mr Hu, I have thought of a way. Why not make an anonymous donation and specify its purpose? It would achieve the same result.” As he spoke, Madam Luosi asked, “What are you discussing?” “That matter my mother spoke of.” Hu briefly explained. “Then how much do you intend to give?” “What do you think?” “In former winters, the padded clothing and congee cost thirty thousand taels. We cannot manage that now. I think ten thousand at the most.” “Good. A fitting middle course. Ten thousand it is.” “Mr Wu can take the money and make the donation. But even an anonymous donor’s real name becomes known to someone. I think we should say it is the old lady’s private savings, given without your knowledge. That is the only position you can defend.” Both men agreed wholeheartedly. The depths of winter had arrived; there could be no delay. Madam Luosi left the table and went upstairs to see to it. In her dressing table lay an account of the private possessions discovered in the concubines’ rooms that day—jewels, gold and silver. She would see whether ten thousand taels could be assembled from them.

zh: “大先生，”乌先生说：“你也不能光做好事，也要为自己打算打算，留起一点儿来。”胡雪岩不作声，过了一会，突然问道：“乌先生，你喜欢字画，趁我没有交出去以前，你挑几件好不好？”原以为乌先生总还要客气一番，要固劝以后才会接受，不道他爽爽快快地答了一个字：“好！”于是胡雪岩拉动一根红色丝绳，便有清越的铃声响起，这是依照西洋法子所设置的叫人铃，通到廊上，也通到搂上，顷之间。来了两个丫头，阿云亦奉了螺蛳太太之命，下楼来探问何事呼唤。“把画箱扛开来！不够亮。”看画不能点烛，阿云交代再来两个人，多点羌手油灯，然后取来钥匙，打开画箱，胡雪岩买这画古董，真假、精粗不分，价高为贵，有个“古董鬼”人人皆知的故事，有人拿了一幅宋画去求售，画是真迹，价钱也还克己，本已可以成交，不道此人说了一句：“胡大先生，这张画我没有赚你的钱，这个价钱是便宜的。”“我这里不赚钱，你到哪里去赚？拿走拿走。我不要占你的便宜。”交易就此告吹。因此，“古董鬼”上门，无不索取高价，成交以后亦必千恩万谢。乌先生对此道是内行，亦替胡雪岩经手买进过好些精品，庆余堂的收藏，大致有所了解。在美孚油灯没有点来以前，他说：“我先看看帖。”
en: “Mr Hu, you cannot think only of charity,” Wu said. “You must consider yourself too and keep something in reserve.” Hu remained silent. After a while he suddenly asked, “You enjoy calligraphy and painting, Mr Wu. Before I hand mine over, would you like to choose a few pieces?” He expected polite refusals and thought he would have to press hard before Wu accepted. Instead, Wu answered immediately with one word: “Yes.” Hu pulled a red silk cord. A clear bell rang: a Western-style servant bell, connected to the corridor and the upper floor. Two maids soon appeared. Madam Luosi also sent A’yun down to ask what was needed. “Bring the picture chests over. There is not enough light.” Candles could not be used for examining paintings. A’yun called for two more servants and additional oil lamps, then fetched the keys and opened the chests. When buying paintings and antiques, Hu had made little distinction between genuine and false, fine and crude. A high price was what mattered to him. Antique dealers all knew a story about this. A man once offered him a Song painting. It was genuine, and the price reasonable. The sale was all but settled when the man said, “Mr Hu, I am making no profit on this. The price is a bargain.” “If you cannot make a profit from me, where can you? Take it away. I do not want to take advantage of you.” The sale fell through. Hence every dealer who came to Hu asked a high price and, after concluding the sale, thanked him profusely. Wu knew this field well and had bought several fine works for him. He was broadly familiar with the Qingyu Hall collection. Before the Meifu kerosene lamps arrived, he said, “Let me look at the calligraphy rubbings first.”

zh: 碑帖俗名“黑老虎”。胡雪岩很兴奋地说：“我有一只‘黑老虎’，真正是‘老虎肉’，三千两银子买的。说实话，我是看中乾隆亲笔写的金字。”“喔，我听说你有部化度寺碑，是唐拓。”乌先生说：“宋拓已经名贵不得了，唐拓我倒要见识见识。”“阿云，”胡雪岩问道：“我那部帖在哪里？”“恐怕是在朱姨太那里。”“喔，”胡雪岩又问：“朱姨太还是在她自己的地方？”“搬到客房里住。”阿云答说：“她原来的地方锁起来了。”“这样说，那部帖一时拿不出来？”“我先去问问朱姨太看。等阿云一定，只见四名丫头，各持一盏白铜底座、玻璃灯罩的美孚油灯，鱼贯而至。书房中顿时明如白昼。胡雪岩便将一串画箱钥匙，交到乌先生手里，说一句：“请你自己动手。”
en: Rubbings from inscribed stelae were commonly called “black tigers.” Hu said excitedly, “I have a black tiger that really is tiger meat. It cost me three thousand taels. To tell the truth, what caught my eye was the gold lettering in the Qianlong Emperor’s own hand.” “I have heard that you own a Tang rubbing of the Huadu Temple Stele. A Song rubbing would already be immensely valuable. I should like to see a Tang one.” “A’yun, where is that album?” “I think it is with Mistress Zhu.” “Oh. Is Mistress Zhu still in her own rooms?” “She has moved into a guest room. Her old rooms are locked.” “Then we cannot get the album just now?” “Let me ask her first.” As soon as A’yun left, four maids filed in, each carrying a Meifu kerosene lamp with a white-copper base and a glass shade. The study became as bright as day. Hu handed Wu the bunch of keys to the picture chests. “Please help yourself.”

zh: 乌先生亦就象处理自己的珍藏一样，先打量画箱，约莫七尺长，四尺宽，三尺高，樟木所制，一共八具，并排摆在北墙下，依照千字文“天地玄黄，宇宙洪荒”编号。钥匙亦是八枚，上镌数字，“一”字当然用来开天宇号画箱，打开一看，上面有一本册子，标明“庆余堂胡氏书画碑帖目录”字样。“这就省事了。”乌先生很高兴地说：“我先看目录。”目录分法书、名画、墨拓三大类，每类又按朝代来分。法书类下第一件是“西晋际机平复帖卷纸本”。乌先生入眼吓一跳，愣在那里说不出话来。“怎么样？”胡雪岩诧异地向。“西晋到现在，少说也有一千五百年了，居然还有纸本留下来！这比王羲之的《兰亭序》还要贵重。王羲之的《兰亭序》原本，唐太宗带到棺村里去了，想不到还有比他再早的真迹，真正眼福不浅。”胡雪岩笑一笑说：“你看了再说。”
en: Wu went about it as though handling his own collection. First he surveyed the chests: about seven chi long, four wide and three high, made of camphorwood. There were eight, arranged side by side against the north wall and labelled with the first eight characters of the Thousand Character Classic: Heaven, Earth, Dark, Yellow, Universe, Cosmos, Vast, Primeval. There were also eight keys, engraved with numbers. Naturally the key numbered one opened the Heaven chest. Inside, on top, lay a booklet entitled Catalogue of Calligraphy, Paintings and Rubbings in the Hu Family Collection of Qingyu Hall. “That makes things easy,” Wu said happily. “I shall read the catalogue first.” It had three main divisions—fine calligraphy, famous paintings and ink rubbings—each subdivided by dynasty. The first calligraphy entry was “Western Jin: Lu Ji, The Pingfu Letter, handscroll on paper.” Wu was so startled that for a moment he could not speak. “What is it?” Hu asked. “At least fifteen hundred years have passed since the Western Jin, and a work on paper has survived! This is more precious than Wang Xizhi’s Preface to the Orchid Pavilion. The original of that went into the coffin with Emperor Taizong of Tang. To find genuine writing earlier still—what extraordinary good fortune for the eyes!” Hu smiled. “Look at it before you say more.”

zh: 于是乌先生小心谨慎地从画箱中净“陆机平复帖卷”取了出来。这个手卷，装演得非常讲究，外面是蓝地花鸟绰丝包衬，羊脂白玉卷轴，珊瑚插签，拔去插签摊了开来，卷前黄绢隔水，一条月白绢签，是宋徽宗御题：“晋陆机平复帖”六字，下铃双龙玺，另外又有一条极旧的绢签题明：“晋平原内史吴郡陆士衡书”。纸呈象牙色，字大五分许，写的是章草，一共九行，细细观玩，却只识得十分之一，不过后面董其昌的一行跋，却是字字皆识：“右军以前，元常以后，唯存此数行，为希代宝。”
en: With great care Wu took out the scroll. Its mounting was exquisite: a blue kesi silk wrapper patterned with birds and flowers, a mutton-fat white jade roller, and a coral fastening pin. He withdrew the pin and unrolled it. At the beginning, over a yellow silk mounting strip, lay a pale-blue silk label inscribed by Emperor Huizong of Song with six Chinese characters: “Jin: Lu Ji’s Pingfu Letter.” Beneath it was a double-dragon seal. Another very old silk label read, “Written by Lu Shiheng of Wu Commandery, Administrator of Pingyuan under the Jin.” The paper was ivory-coloured, the characters about half a cun high. There were nine lines of zhangcao, an early cursive script. Studying them closely, Wu could recognize only a tenth. But every word of Dong Qichang’s later inscription was clear: “Before the General of the Right, after Yuanchang, only these few lines remain: a treasure rare through the ages.”

zh: 董其昌的字，乌先生见过好几幅，细细观察，判定不真，但不便直言论断，只将那个手卷卷了起来。胡雪岩便问：“怎么样？”“似乎有点疑问。”“你的眼光不错，是西贝货。”胡雪岩指着目录说：“你看几件真东西。”原来这些字画，胡雪岩曾请行家鉴别过，在目录上做了记号。记号分三种，单圈是假货，双圈则在真假疑似之间，或者虽假也很值钱，譬如宋人临仿的唐画之类，至于没有疑问的真迹，则印上一朵小小的梅花为记，在目录上，大概只有五分之一。于是，乌先生挑了一部“苏氏一门十二帖”来看，内中收了苏老泉、东坡、子由及东坡幼子叔党的十二封信，入眼即知不假。“不必看原件，我在目录上挑好了。大先生，你打算送我几件？”“你自己说。”“你要我说，有梅花印记的我都要。”乌先生紧接着又说：“我是替你保管。大先生，你相信不相信我？”乌先生的本意如此，是胡雪岩所意料不到的，但这便是私下藏匿资财，有欠光明磊落。他考虑了一会，断然决然地说：“乌先生，这不必。我仍旧送你几件，你再细细挑。”乌先生是一番好意，胡雪岩既然不受，他亦不便再多说什么，但仍旧存着能为他保全一份算一份的想法，因而除了“苏氏一门十二帖”以外，另外选了一部“宋徽宗瘦金体书千字文”，一幅董源的“风雨出蛰龙图”，一个赵孟頫的“竹林七贤图”手卷。估计这四件书画，就值上万银子。
en: Wu had seen several examples of Dong Qichang’s hand. Careful comparison convinced him that this inscription was not genuine. Reluctant to say so outright, he merely rolled the scroll up. “Well?” Hu asked. “There seem to be some grounds for doubt.” “Your eye is good. It is a fake.” Hu pointed at the catalogue. “Look at a few genuine things.” Experts had already examined the collection for him and marked the catalogue. There were three kinds of mark. A single circle meant a forgery; a double circle indicated uncertain authenticity, or a copy valuable in its own right, such as a Song copy of a Tang painting. Works accepted without question as genuine bore a little plum-blossom stamp. These made up about a fifth of the catalogue. Wu next selected Twelve Letters of the Su Family, containing letters by Su Laoquan, Dongpo, Ziyou and Dongpo’s youngest son Shudang. One glance showed they were genuine. “I need not inspect every original. I can choose from the catalogue. How many pieces do you intend to give me?” “You decide.” “Then I should like everything bearing a plum-blossom stamp.” He immediately added, “To keep safe for you. Mr Hu, do you trust me?” Hu had not anticipated his real purpose. But this would mean secretly concealing assets and would not be honourable. After considering, he answered firmly, “There is no need, Mr Wu. I shall still give you a few pieces. Choose carefully.” Wu had meant well, but could say no more when Hu refused. Still hoping to preserve as much as possible for him, he selected, besides the Su letters, Emperor Huizong’s Thousand Character Classic in Slender Gold Script, Dong Yuan’s Dragon Emerging from Hibernation in Wind and Rain, and a handscroll of The Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove by Zhao Mengfu. Together, these four works were estimated to be worth more than ten thousand taels.

zh: 于是丫头们在胡雪岩指挥之下，开启三只画箱，将送乌先生的字画找齐捆扎妥当。螺蛳太太与阿云亦相继而回，那部“唐拓化度寺碑”一时无从找起，也就罢了。捐给善堂的一万银子，已经凑齐，都是银票，即时点交乌先生收讫，然后摆开桌子，酒食消夜。“摆三双杯筷！”胡雪岩关照阿云：“一起坐。”这是指螺蛳太太而言。她视乌先生如亲属长辈，不必有礼仪上的男女之别。入座以后，用一小杯绿色的西洋薄荷酒，陪乌先生喝陈年花雕，胡雪岩仍旧照例喝睡前的药酒。“老七搬到客房里去了？”胡雪岩问。胡雪岩有时管朱姨太叫老七。“她自己提出来的，”螺蛳太太说：“她说，平时大家热热闹闹的，突然之间，冷冷清清，她会睡不着。”
en: Under Hu’s direction, the maids opened three chests, found all the works intended for Wu and tied them into a bundle. Madam Luosi and A’yun returned one after the other. The Tang rubbing of the Huadu Temple Stele could not be located for the moment, so they let it pass. The ten thousand taels for the charitable hall had been assembled, all in banknotes. They were counted out and handed to Wu at once. Then the table was laid for wine and supper. “Three cups and sets of chopsticks,” Hu told A’yun. “Sit with us.” He meant Madam Luosi. She regarded Wu as an elder of her own family, so there was no need for the formal separation of men and women. Seated with them, she sipped green Western mint liqueur from a little glass while Wu drank aged Huadiao. Hu took his usual medicinal wine before bed. “Has Old Seven moved to a guest room?” he asked. He sometimes called Mistress Zhu Old Seven. “At her own request. She said that after all the bustle and company, she would not be able to sleep in such sudden emptiness.”

zh: 胡雪岩点点头，眼看乌先生，示意他开口。于是乌先生为螺蛳太太细谈这天在周少棠家的情形，最后提出郑俊生的见解。“不会的。”螺蛳太太说：“大先生哪天住在哪里，都在皇历上记下来的。我查过，住在朱姨太那里，最后一次是两个多月以前。至于……”她本来想开个小小的玩笑，说胡雪岩与朱姨太是否私下燕好过，可就不知道了。但这时候都没有说笑话的心情，所以把话咽住了。“还是小心点的好。再等一个月看，没有害喜的样子再送到周家也还不迟。”“也好。”螺蛳太太问：“这一个多月住在哪里呢？”“住在我那里好了。”“这就更加可以放心了。”胡雪岩作个切断的手势，“这件事就算这样子定规了。”“我知道了。”螺蛳太太说：“我会安排。”
en: Hu nodded and looked at Wu, signalling him to speak. Wu described the day’s events at Zhou’s house and ended with Zheng’s concern. “That will not be the case,” Madam Luosi said. “Every night the master spends in each room is marked in the almanac. I checked. His last night with Mistress Zhu was more than two months ago. As for…” She had been about to joke that she could not know whether Hu and Mistress Zhu had been intimate in private since. But nobody was in a joking mood, so she swallowed the words. “Better to be careful. There is no harm in waiting another month and sending her to Zhou’s only when she shows no sign of pregnancy.” “Very well. Where will she stay for this month or more?” “At my house,” Wu said. “Then we can be still easier in our minds.” Hu made a decisive gesture. “That settles it.” “I understand,” Madam Luosi said. “I shall arrange everything.”

zh: 于是要谈肺腑之言，根本之计了。首先是乌先生发问：“大先生，你自己觉得这个跟斗是栽定了？”“不认栽又怎么样？”“我不认栽！”螺蛳太太接口说道：“路是人走出来的。”“年纪不饶人啊！”胡雪岩很冷静地接着说道：“栽了这个跟斗，能够站起来，就不容易了，哪里还谈得到重新去走一条路出来。”“不然，能立直，就能走路。”乌先生说：“大先生，你不要气馁，东山再起，事在人为。”“乌先生，你给我打气，我很感激。不过，说实话，凡事说来容易做来难。你说东山再起，我就不晓得东山在哪里？”“你尽说泄气的话！”螺蛳太太是恨胡雪岩不争气的神情，“你从前不是这样子的！”“从前是从前，现在是现在。”胡雪岩也有些激动了，“我现在是革了职的一品老百姓，再下去会不会抄家都还不晓得，别的就不必说了。”提到抄家，乌先生又有一句心里的话要说，“大先生，你总要留点本钱的。”胡雪岩不作声，螺蛳太太却触动了心事，盘算了好一会，正要发言，不道胡雪岩先开了口。
en: Now they were to speak frankly of their deepest concerns and fundamental plans. Wu began. “Mr Hu, do you believe this fall is final?” “What can I do but accept it?” “I do not accept it!” Madam Luosi put in. “A road is made by those who walk it.” Hu replied calmly, “Age does not spare a man. After a fall like this, getting back on my feet would be difficult enough. How could I talk of making a new road?” “Not so. If you can stand upright, you can walk,” Wu said. “Do not lose heart. A comeback depends on human effort.” “I appreciate your encouragement. But honestly, everything is easier said than done. You speak of rising again from the Eastern Mountain, but I do not even know where that mountain is.” “All this dispirited talk!” Madam Luosi resented his lack of resolve. “You were never like this before.” “Before was before. Now is now.” Hu too grew agitated. “I am a commoner of the first rank, dismissed from office. I do not even know whether confiscation will follow. There is no point discussing anything else.” Mention of confiscation brought another earnest appeal from Wu. “You must keep some capital in reserve.” Hu said nothing. Madam Luosi, however, was prompted to think. She considered for some time and was about to speak when Hu spoke first.

zh: “你不服气，我倒替你想到一个主意。”胡雪岩对螺蛳太太说：“有样生意你不妨试一试。““莫非要我回老本行？”螺蛳太太以为胡雪岩是劝她仍旧做绣货生意。“不是。”胡雪岩答说：“你如果有兴致，不妨同应春合作，在上海去炒地皮、造弄堂房子，或者同洋人合伙，开一家专卖外国首饰、衣料、家具的洋行。”“不错，这两样行当，都可以发挥罗四姐的长处。”乌先生深表赞成，“大先生栽了跟斗，罗四姐来闯一番事业，也算失之东隅，收之桑榆。”“以后我要靠你了。”胡雪岩开玩笑自嘲：“想不到我老来会‘吃拖鞋饭’。”“难听不难听？”螺蛳太太白了他一眼。乌先生与胡雪岩都笑了。乌先生道：“不过，这两种行当，都不是小本生意。大先生，趁现在自己还能作主的时候，要早早筹划。”这依旧是劝胡雪岩疏散财物、寄顿他处之意。胡雪岩不愿意这么做，不过他觉得有提醒螺蛳太太的必要。“你自己的私房，自己料理。”胡雪岩说：“我想，你要干那两样行当，本钱应该早就有了吧？”“没有现款。现款存在阜康，将来能拿回多少，不晓得。首饰倒有一点，不过脱手也难。”“你趁早拿出来，托乌先生带到上海，交给应春去想办法。”
en: “If you refuse to accept defeat, I have an idea for you. There is a business you could try.” “You want me to return to my old trade?” She thought he meant embroidery. “No. If you are interested, you could join Yingchun in Shanghai to speculate in land and build houses in lanes. Or you could form a partnership with foreigners and open a firm specializing in foreign jewellery, dress materials and furniture.” “Exactly. Either business would make use of Luo Sijie’s strengths,” Wu said approvingly. “If Mr Hu has fallen, she can make a career of her own. What is lost at sunrise may be regained at sunset.” “I shall have to depend on you from now on.” Hu joked at his own expense. “Who would have thought that in my old age I should live on ‘slipper rice’—supported by a woman?” “What a dreadful thing to say!” She gave him a look. Both men laughed. Wu continued, “But neither business can be started with a small sum. While you still have some control, you should make arrangements early.” Again he was urging Hu to disperse his assets and lodge them elsewhere. Hu would not do that, but thought Madam Luosi should be reminded of something. “See to your own private savings. Surely you have long had enough capital for either venture?” “No ready money. My cash is at Fukang. Who knows how much I shall recover? I have some jewellery, but that is difficult to sell too.” “Take it out soon and ask Mr Wu to carry it to Shanghai. Yingchun can find a way of disposing of it.”

zh: “东西不在手里。”“在哪里？”胡雪岩说：“你是寄在什么人手里？”“金洞桥朱家。”一听这话，胡雪岩不作声，脸色显得根深沉。见此光景，螺蛳太太心便往下一沉，知道不大妥当。“怎么了？”她说：“朱家不是老亲吗？朱大少奶奶是极好的人。”“朱大少奶奶人好，可是她家的老太太是吃人不吐骨头的角色。”“啊！”螺蛳太太大吃一惊，“朱老太太吃素念经，而且她们家也是有名殷实的人家，莫非……”“莫非会吞没你的东西？”胡雪岩问得多少有些调侃。“是啊！我不相信她会起黑心。”“她家本来就是起黑心发的财……”“这话，”乌先生插嘴说道：“大概有段故事在内。大先生，是不是？”“不错，我来讲给你们听。”
en: “I do not have it with me.” “Where is it? Have you left it in someone’s keeping?” “With the Zhu family at Jindong Bridge.” Hu fell silent, his expression darkening. At the sight, Madam Luosi’s heart sank. Something must be wrong. “What is it? Are the Zhus not old family connections? Their eldest son’s wife is an excellent woman.” “She is. But the old lady in that household would devour a person without leaving a bone.” “Oh!” Madam Luosi was alarmed. “Old Madam Zhu is a devout vegetarian, always chanting sutras. And the family is famously well off. Surely…” “Surely she would not swallow up your property?” Hu asked, with a trace of mockery. “Yes. I cannot believe she would be so wicked.” “Wickedness was how her family made its fortune in the first place…” Wu interrupted. “There must be a story behind that. Is there not, Mr Hu?” “Indeed. Let me tell it to you.”
